public_rationale: The claim is that, apart from hyperscalers buying NVIDIA GPUs from cash flow, no part of the AI industry runs on revenue, and every part runs on some kind of subsidy. The core of this holds for the biggest links he describes. In 2025 OpenAI spent $34 billion against $13 billion of revenue, and it relied on investor capital to cover the gap. But the universal 'none' and 'every single part' does not hold. Gamma, a generative AI app with more than $100 million in annual recurring revenue, said in November 2025 that it had been profitable for more than two years. A profitable company covers its costs from revenue. One could argue Gamma benefits indirectly from below-cost model pricing. Counting that as 'subsidy' would make the claim true by definition. So the main thrust is supported and the absolute wording is contradicted.
limitations: The result turns on whether 'parts' means whole segments or individual companies, and on how broadly 'subsidy' is read.

our_interpretation: Reading, following the reviewers: apart from hyperscaler GPU purchases funded from cash flow, every part of the AI industry depends on outside capital (venture money, debt, investor support) rather than its own revenue to cover ongoing costs.
The claim is universal ('none', 'every single part'). In context the 'parts' are links in his chain: GPU buyers and data centers, model providers, and AI startups.
Target period: an ongoing state with no named period, so calendar 2025 up to the post date (2025-01-01 to 2025-12-29), the latest period public evidence covers.
Indirect subsidy through below-cost model pricing is noted, but not treated as making a profitable company 'fueled by subsidy', since that would make the claim true by definition.
criteria.support_condition: The main parts of the chain (model providers, neoclouds, AI startups) cover their ongoing costs with outside capital rather than revenue, and no meaningful non-hyperscaler AI business covers its costs from revenue.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Meaningful non-hyperscaler AI businesses are shown to cover their ongoing costs from customer revenue (for example, sustained profitability) during the period.
